FEASIBLE-CENTRE REGION on a 194x194 grid of pitch 0.01998 (<= 0.02) x 36 tilts; both verdicts carry the Lipschitz margin m =

container has area 7.8310, so at most 9 more unit squares fit — the budget is 5, so this alone does not kill the node.

PANEL G is the GEOMETRY of the hypothesis: the container, the hypothesis squares with their certified cores, and the shaded set of centres where one further unit square can still be placed at SOME tilt. Nothing in panel G comes from an LP; it is what the case hypothesis alone
forces. This is the panel to read for a shortcut.

PANEL S is the LP RELAXATION's dual support: a fractional measure, one placement per column, shaded by dual weight. Its squares OVERLAP each other and sometimes the hypothesis — that is the relaxation's slack, not a packing, and a column drawn red is one the geometry of panel G

PANEL N is a REAL PACKING: the nearest configuration of eleven pairwise interior-disjoint unit squares to this node's support, minimised over its own side s*. If s* > s0 the configuration does not fit in the certified container; the square names are the labels used everywhere

outlines beside a lane tag are WITNESSED free meeters (sampled poses), with how far each reaches into the cell.
